review_notes:
I read all 242 lines of the file. I also checked the definitions it depends on: `axisHeight`, `axisDirection`, `height_axisDirection`, `axisHeight_add` and `axisHeight_zero` in Axis.lean; `Site` and `stepVector` in Model.lean; `RegenerationWord` in Words.lean; and `annealed_exit_band` in HittingWords.lean. In Mathlib I checked `Finset.sum_apply` and `Finset.sum_neg_distrib`; both are simp lemmas generated with `to_additive`. I also read the `omega` docstring to see which logical forms it accepts.

Most proofs are already fairly direct: case splits on the `Bool` field followed by `simp`, or short `filter_upwards` blocks. I report two small but real simplifications.

Candidates I looked at and rejected:
- `annealed_axis_exit`: removing its `by_cases` would mean relying on `omega` to handle an implication hypothesis, and the `omega` docstring does not clearly say it does that.
- `axis_barriers_disjoint` and `axis_word_last_step`: the possible changes there (a term-mode proof, or `rwa` instead of `rw ... at hf; exact hf`) only save characters or come down to taste.
- `opposed_departure_band`: this proof is complex, but it is not clear that any change would make it easier to read.

I have not compiled either replacement. How confident I am in each one is stated in its finding.

findings.excerpt:
classical
  induction s using Finset.induction_on with
  | empty => simp [axisHeight_zero]
  | @insert i s hi ih => simp [Finset.sum_insert hi,axisHeight_add,ih]
findings.problem: `axisHeight e x` is just one coordinate of `x`, possibly negated (`if e.2 then x e.1 else -(x e.1)`). So the lemma says that a coordinate of a sum is the sum of the coordinates. The current proof instead rebuilds additivity by induction on the finset. That needs a `classical` block, a named `@insert` case and two separate simp calls. It also hides the reason the lemma holds.
findings.proposed_change:
Use the same coordinate-wise proof as the neighbouring lemmas `axisHeight_neg`, `axisHeight_opposite` and `axisHeight_step_self`:
```lean
lemma axisHeight_sum {d : ℕ} {ι : Type*} (e : Step d) (s : Finset ι) (f : ι → Site d) :
    axisHeight e (∑ i ∈ s, f i) = ∑ i ∈ s, axisHeight e (f i) := by
  rcases e with ⟨j,b⟩
  cases b <;> simp [axisHeight, Finset.sum_apply]
```
`Finset.sum_apply` moves the coordinate evaluation inside the sum. In the `false` case, the simp lemma `Finset.sum_neg_distrib` turns the sum of negations on the right into the negation of the sum. This replacement has not been compiled.
findings.benefit: The proof now says directly why the lemma is true: evaluating a coordinate commutes with finite sums. It matches the `rcases`/`cases b <;> simp [axisHeight]` pattern the reader has just seen in the three lemmas above it, and it drops the `classical` and induction scaffolding.

findings.proposed_change:
Replace line 57 with a single cast transfer of the whole conjunction:

`norm_cast` rewrites casts throughout a proposition, including under `∧`. This replacement has not been compiled.
findings.benefit: The last step now reads as one fact: the hypothesis is the goal after removing casts. There is no repeated bracketed sub-tactic, which makes this proof match the sibling lemma `axisHeight_wordEnd` (which ends in `exact_mod_cast h`).
